Graphs

Source: R/graph_network.R
GenericGraphClass.Rd

Graph() displays an undirected graph and DiGraph() a directed one: vertices (by default Dot()s) joined by edges (by default Line()s). An updater keeps the edges attached to the vertices, so moving a vertex drags its edges along.

Vertices are identified by their names (numbers are converted to strings). Look up a vertex with g$get(1) or g$vertices[["1"]] and an edge with g$get(c(1, 2)). Methods: add_vertices(), remove_vertices(), add_edges(), remove_edges() and change_layout(); g$animate$change_layout("circular") animates the new layout. g$animate$add_vertices() and g$animate$add_edges() return Create() animations of the new mobjects, and g$animate$remove_vertices() and g$animate$remove_edges() return Uncreate() animations of the removed ones; choose another animation with g$animate(animation = FadeIn).

Usage

Graph(
  vertices,
  edges,
  labels = FALSE,
  label_fill_color = BLACK,
  layout = "spring",
  layout_scale = 2,
  layout_config = NULL,
  vertex_type = Dot,
  vertex_config = NULL,
  vertex_mobjects = NULL,
  edge_type = Line,
  partitions = NULL,
  root_vertex = NULL,
  edge_config = NULL
)

DiGraph(
  vertices,
  edges,
  labels = FALSE,
  label_fill_color = BLACK,
  layout = "spring",
  layout_scale = 2,
  layout_config = NULL,
  vertex_type = Dot,
  vertex_config = NULL,
  vertex_mobjects = NULL,
  edge_type = Line,
  partitions = NULL,
  root_vertex = NULL,
  edge_config = NULL
)

Arguments

vertices

Vector or list of vertex names.

edges

List of vertex pairs, such as list(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)), or a two column matrix.

labels

TRUE labels vertices with their names via MathTex(); a named list maps vertex names to label mobjects.

label_fill_color

Color of the labels made for labels = TRUE.

layout

A layout name ("spring", "circular", "kamada_kawai", "planar", "random", "shell", "spectral", "spiral", "tree", "partite"), a named list of positions, or a function function(graph, scale, ...) returning such a list. The layouts follow networkx; "planar" draws a planar graph without crossings (an error for other graphs) and can place vertices differently from networkx, which picks some vertices in hash order.

layout_scale

Half width of the generated layouts.

layout_config

Named list of extra arguments for the layout, for example list(nlist = ...) for "shell", list(root_vertex = 1, vertex_spacing = c(1, 1)) for "tree", list(dist = ...) for "kamada_kawai", or list(seed = 1) for "spring" and "random".

vertex_type

Constructor (or R6 generator) for vertices.

vertex_config

Named list of arguments for vertex_type; entries named by a vertex are used for that vertex only.

vertex_mobjects

Named list of mobjects used as vertices.

edge_type

Constructor (or R6 generator) for edges.

partitions

Partitions for the "partite" layout.

root_vertex

Root for the "tree" layout.

edge_config

Named list of arguments for edge_type; entries named "u-v" apply to the edge from u to v. Inside a vertex name, escape each - and each backslash with a backslash when the plain form would name several edges. For DiGraph(), a tip_config entry (globally or per edge) styles the tips.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
g <- Graph(1:4, list(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(3, 4), c(1, 3), c(1, 4)), layout = "circular")
g$get(1)$move_to(c(1, 1, 0))
} # }
